progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: Cells contain DNA; DNA carries inherited information (Year 11 Biology). Chromosomes, genes and alleles get plain meanings in the lesson.
progression.startsWith: Every Cavendish banana plant is a clone, and TR4 is spreading.
progression.stopsAfter: Explaining how sexual and asexual reproduction support continuity and judging which suits stable or changing conditions.
progression.nextLesson: B2: how animals bring sperm and egg together.

teaching.task: Explain how each reproduction method supports continuity and choose between them for given conditions.
teaching.causalExplanation: Continuity needs DNA passed on and offspring that survive to reproduce; asexual copying is fast but clones share weaknesses; gamete fusion creates new allele combinations so some individuals may survive change.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Real Cavendish and TR4 story, strawberry mechanisms, building an HSC compare answer on screen.
teaching.openingDecision: Why would sharing one set of DNA be risky for bananas?
teaching.understandingCheck: Choose a strategy for a stable pond, a lone island plant and a crop facing new disease, with reasons.
teaching.curriculumScope: Explain the mechanisms of reproduction that ensure continuity of a species by analysing sexual and asexual methods (BIO12-12, Module 5 IQ1).

design.visualSystem: Explainer engine: warm paper stage, handwritten Caveat headings, amber doodle layer, painted botanical plates with coded cell animations.
design.transitionPlan: Banana bunch duplicates to clones then cuts to plantation; generation chain pans; montage panels slide in; scene crossfades with settle.
